sessionName: Week 2 - Value proposition for PE-backed CFOs
summary: George Berrington worked with Paul and Rebecca on the value proposition for CFOs of PE portfolio companies, building on the week 1 ICP. We agreed a message centred on cash and EBITDA ahead of covenant tests, backed by audited savings. Point of view content still needs agreement.

discussion.keyPoints: Rebecca said CFOs care most about savings that land in the P&L this financial year and can be shown to the board and lenders.
Paul had three examples, including a logistics client with £2.4m annualised savings on £31m spend. Rebecca warned that unverified figures have been challenged before.
Current website talks about 'strategic sourcing excellence', which Paul agreed means nothing to a CFO.

recommendations.recommendation: Lead with: we deliver 6% to 9% savings on addressable spend, signed off by your finance team, within 12 weeks.
Only use savings figures verified by the client finance team, starting with the logistics client at £2.4m on £31m spend.
Rewrite the website and pitch deck around three messages: cash, covenant headroom, audited savings.
Publish a point of view arguing that savings claimed without finance sign-off are worthless.

actions.action: Get written sign-off from the logistics client to use their figures

nextFocus: Plan how to generate demand from PE operating partners and CFOs.
nextPreparation: Rebecca to list all lead sources from the last 12 months.

tests.question: What savings range do we promise in our value proposition?
Which case study figures can we use?
expectedFacts: verified by the client finance team

tests.question: Is the point of view piece on unverified savings agreed?
